F6_fabricated_metrics_found_and_fixed_20: Before starting Phase C, re-checked the actual evaluation mechanism (V2DevelopmentGateEvaluator in research/v2_development_gate.py) and found it returned HARDCODED CONSTANTS for cagr_pct, max_drawdown_pct, sharpe_ratio, and sortino_ratio - literally `12.5 if gate_pass else -5.0` etc, not computed from the backtest's actual equity curve at all. This is the exact 'governance certificate that looks rigorous but isn't' failure this project's own audit history warns about, live in the mechanism meant to gate Phase C admissions. Fixed: now computed via MetricsEngine (the same real computation Phase B validation used), reusing res.equity_curve from the same backtest run. Verified: 275/275 tests still pass (no test had asserted the old fake values), clean on ruff and mypy. SECOND DEFECT FOUND IN THE SAME FILE: the gate also reimplemented R-multiple calculation locally instead of using TradeRecord.r_multiple (the engine's official F2/F2b-fixed field) - it fabricated a fake 5%-of-entry-price stop when stop_loss_level was None and scored degenerate risk distances as 0.0 instead of excluding them, exactly the F2/F2b defect pattern reintroduced in a second code path with zero test coverage proving it correct. Fixed: now uses t.r_multiple directly, excludes unmeasurable trades from the mean rather than inventing values for them, added r_multiple_coverage_pct to the scorecard and a rejection reason when coverage < 90% (mirrors MetricsEngine's INSUFFICIENT_R_COVERAGE handling). RELATED, NOT YET FIXED: research/benchmark_suite.py has the same defect class - hardcoded 'baseline benchmark' returns (BENCH-NIFTY50-BH: 12.5, BENCH-EQUAL-WEIGHT: 11.2, etc.) presented as comparison baselines but never actually computed from real backtests of those benchmarks. Not fixed because it doesn't block Phase C hypothesis evaluation directly; flagged for whoever next touches benchmark comparison.
F7_fee_dominated_micro_positions_found_a: With F6 fixed, the first real gate run showed ALL FOUR strategies failing with strongly negative net_expectancy_r (-0.54 to -0.87) despite two (TrendPullback, MomentumRS) showing POSITIVE total P&L - investigated the contradiction rather than reporting it. Traced to STOP_LOSS exits averaging -1.627R (not ~-1.0R), worst case -31.5R. Pulled actual trades: all 15 worst-R trades had total risk (risk_per_share x quantity) between Rs 0.48 and Rs 1.90, every one losing ~Rs 14-17 regardless of price direction (one exit price was even ABOVE entry) - the flat DP/brokerage charge, not a trading loss. Root cause: RiskBasedSizingCalculator's cash-fitting loop (research/sizing.py) had no floor - with cash nearly exhausted (routine with several concurrent positions open), it shrank positions to 1 share rather than rejecting. 149/948 TrendPullbackV2 trades (15.7%) had total risk under Rs 30. FIXED: sizing now rejects (POSITION_TOO_SMALL_RELATIVE_TO_COSTS) when total risk can't clear 10x the trade's own estimated transaction cost (or Rs 200, whichever is larger) - derived from cost structure, not fitted to any result. Added 2 hand-computed regression tests (tests/unit/test_r_multiple_and_sizing.py): cash-starved rejection, and adequately-funded trades still sizing correctly (proving the fix doesn't over-reject). Full suite: 277 passed (was 275), clean on ruff/mypy.

phase_b_run_2026_08_06.root_cause_DIAGNOSED_not_an_engine_bug: v2_strategies.py builds every SignalIntent with max_holding_days=getattr(self, 'max_holding_days', None). Only MeanReversionV2Strategy.__init__ ever sets self.max_holding_days (=5). The other three never set it, so it silently resolves to None - no time-based exit and no profit target, only a stop-loss. Exit breakdowns confirm: STOP_LOSS 90-92%, END_OF_BACKTEST 8-15%, zero target/time exits. A winner that never hits its stop rides uncapped to the literal end of a multi-year backtest, producing 30-60x payoff ratios on the tiny surviving minority.
phase_b_run_2026_08_06.RESOLVED_2026_08_06: Derived max_holding_days from sourced convention BEFORE re-running the backtest, not fitted to results: TrendPullbackV2/BreakoutConfirmV2 = 20 sessions (swing-trading pullback/breakout-continuation convention, commonly cited as 2-4 weeks; also matches each strategy's own existing 20-session parameter). MomentumRSV2 = 63 sessions, set equal to rs_lookback (also 63), mirroring Jegadeesh & Titman (1993)'s matched J=K formation/holding convention (their most-cited combination is 6-month/6-month). Added as a ParameterOrigin entry (category MARKET_CONVENTION) on each strategy, same audit trail as every other parameter. This changed each strategy's config_hash; every test that pinned the old hash was updated to the recomputed value (test_m3b_2_pipeline.py, test_m3b_2_2_accounting.py, test_m3b_3_decision_gate.py, test_m3b_3_1_reconciliation.py, test_m3b_4_final_revision.py).

INCIDENT 2026-08-06, ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED (updated from earlier note in this file which said root cause was not found - it has since been found): the configured PostgreSQL store was found empty twice in one session. Root cause: tests/integration/test_db_postgres.py connected to settings.database_url (the real research database, not an isolated test DB) and ran Base.metadata.drop_all() at setup, teardown, AND mid-test in test_alembic_migration_upgrade_path - every ordinary `pytest tests/` run destroyed the real data. Confirmed by reproducing the second wipe immediately after a pytest run in this session.

Fix chain (3 bugs, first 2 previously invisible because they cancelled out): (1) added isolated POSTGRES_TEST_DB=tradecraft_test in config.py with a hard runtime refusal if it ever equals POSTGRES_DB; (2) alembic/env.py's get_url() unconditionally returned settings.database_url, ignoring any Config.set_main_option override - fixed to check config.get_main_option('sqlalchemy.url') first; (3) alembic.ini had a stale hardcoded sqlalchemy.url with the wrong password, invisible only because of bug (2) - blanked out; (4) once (2) was fixed, the test fixture's str(engine.url) turned out to mask the password as '***' by default in this SQLAlchemy version - fixed to use url.render_as_string(hide_password=False). Verified: full pytest tests/ run leaves the real database's 18-table schema unchanged (direct \dt before/after), all 6 previously-broken test_db_postgres.py tests now pass.

This standing risk is CLOSED, not worked around: pytest tests/ is now safe to run repeatedly and will never touch the real research database again. Recovery for both wipes: alembic upgrade head + full data backfill re-run, verified via direct SQL query.
